issues.title: [Self-hosted] Refresh container runtimes and support security upgrades without regenerating profiles
issues.body:
Related: #3233 (outdated OpenVPN image). This report covers other self-hosted components and the upgrade workflow.

An audit of an existing Linux/amd64 self-hosted deployment on 2026-11-01 found outdated container userspace and embedded runtimes. Updating the VPS packages alone does not update them. Please refresh the server images and provide a supported security-upgrade path that preserves existing server/client identities and profiles.

### Observed versions

These are runtime observations from that deployment, cross-checked against AmneziaVPN **5.0.3.0, commit `de93650a90739b87bb47a632872ea9d0adc9412f`**, and the referenced parent-image sources. They are not a claim that every fresh installation using mutable `latest` tags has identical contents.

| Component | Observed before remediation | Maintenance gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Xray | Alpine 3.15.11; Xray 26.7.28 / Go 1.26.5; OpenSSL 1.1.1w | The [5.0.3 installer Dockerfile](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/de93650a90739b87bb47a632872ea9d0adc9412f/client/server_scripts/xray/Dockerfile) pins Alpine 3.15 and Xray 26.7.28. An APK upgrade within the old branch does not migrate the base or replace the pinned Xray release. |
| AmneziaWG | Alpine 3.19.9; tools `v3.1.20260812`; static daemon built with Go 1.25.12 | The [parent Dockerfile](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amneziawg-go/blob/b5928efb6ca19f0153958460c3d141f04abc5c2e/Dockerfile) still builds with Go 1.25.12. Refreshing only the runtime base leaves the old Go/C runtime inside the static executable. |
| AmneziaDNS | Unbound 1.22.0, built with OpenSSL 3.3.2 | The [installer inherits `mvance/unbound:latest`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/de93650a90739b87bb47a632872ea9d0adc9412f/client/server_scripts/dns/Dockerfile). Updating Debian's libssl package does not replace Unbound's private embedded OpenSSL. Later [Unbound security advisories](https://nlnetlabs.nl/projects/unbound/security-advisories/) include fixes absent from 1.22.0. |
| MTProxy | Debian 12; libssl3 `3.0.19-1~deb12u2`, libc6 `2.36-9+deb12u13` | Newer vendor security packages were available. The [native parent](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/MTProxy/blob/512bc66f07787afc664b35bb88abb1118574a475/Dockerfile) copies the daemon separately, so runtime packages can be refreshed without rebuilding the proxy. |
| SOCKS5 | Minimal image with Debian glibc `2.36-9+deb12u9`, without a full package database | Checking only the BusyBox/3proxy versions misses the bundled loader/libc. Please include these files in the image's dependency inventory and update process. |

For AWG, this was verified beyond version strings: the official amd64 parent manifest `sha256:c68009d33df3aef4654db72bf1a7880cfa0a631fe866c50d9ae3dd34ddd7c13a` contained daemon SHA-256 `6177066f0e35b1cb44945136d9a10841dd3ce30fdf16009c9a815cd943a982fe`, matching the deployed binary. Its registry-attached build provenance points to source commit `b5928efb6ca19f0153958460c3d141f04abc5c2e`. This is a provenance/byte match, not a claim of independent signature verification.

### Requested behavior

1. Publish refreshed server images on supported bases, rebuilding static Go components with a supported, patched toolchain as well as updating OS libraries.
2. Provide a documented **upgrade-existing-server** operation that preserves keys, peer/client profiles, ports, DNS settings and persistent data. Keep security upgrades distinct from removing/reprovisioning a protocol, and make replacement of administrator-managed components explicit.
3. Expose installed component/toolchain versions and image identities, and periodically rebuild/check images against vendor advisories. Include embedded libraries and scratch-image dependencies, not only the package-manager inventory.
4. Validate actual protocol readiness after upgrading, with rollback, and document host-kernel updates separately from container updates.

### Local validation of the approach

Manual remediation retained the existing key

issues.title: fix(daemon): bracket IPv6 server endpoint in UAPI config
issues.body:
Fixes #2607

## Problem
When a WireGuard/AmneziaWG config uses an IPv6 endpoint (e.g. `Endpoint = [2001:db8::2]:51820`), the daemon fails to bring the tunnel up: the UAPI `set` returns `-22` (EINVAL) and the connection drops right after connecting.

In `updatePeer()` the server address ends up in `m_serverIpv4AddrIn` even when it is an IPv6 literal, so it is written to the IPC stream without brackets:

```
endpoint=2001:db8::2:51820
```

The userspace WireGuard implementation cannot parse that as `host:port`.

## Fix
If the address in `m_serverIpv4AddrIn` contains `:` and is not already bracketed, wrap it in `[...]` before appending the port. IPv4 addresses and hostnames are unchanged. The existing `m_serverIpv6AddrIn` branch already brackets correctly and is left as is.

The same pattern exists in all three desktop daemons, so the fix is applied to:
- `client/platforms/linux/daemon/wireguardutilslinux.cpp`
- `client/platforms/macos/daemon/wireguardutilsmacos.cpp`
- `client/platforms/windows/daemon/wireguardutilswindows.cpp`

## Testing
The bug was reproduced on Linux Mint 22.3 with AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 (IPv6 endpoint fails with IPC error -22; the same server over IPv4 works). I have not built the client with this patch yet. The macOS and Windows changes are the same code change and have not been tested on those platforms.

issues.title: Android: auto-reconnect when the AmneziaWG tunnel stalls after idle (connection watchdog)
issues.body:
AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.1 (AWG 3.1), Android 16, OnePlus 15.
Self-hosted AmneziaWG, mobile network (Russia), battery set
to "Unrestricted" for AmneziaVPN.

Problem
After the phone has been idle with the screen off, the tunnel
sometimes stalls: nothing works (Telegram, browser) until I
manually disconnect and reconnect in AmneziaVPN. It happens
several times a day. A manual reconnect always fixes it
immediately.

What we see on the server side
We captured traffic on our server during these episodes. While
the tunnel is stalled, no packets from the phone reach the server
at all — no handshake initiation, nothing, for 4–44 minutes.
Other devices on the same server work normally at the same time.
Typical sequence: the phone wakes up, sends a few data packets
with the old session from a new NAT port (the mobile operator
changed it during sleep), the server drops them (keys older than
180 s), and then the phone never sends a new handshake. A manual
reconnect opens a new socket, the handshake completes in ~0.1 s,
and traffic flows right away.

Feature request: connection watchdog
An option to detect a stalled tunnel and restart it automatically,
for example:
- if the latest handshake is older than ~140 s
  (REKEY_AFTER_TIME + KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT + REKEY_TIMEOUT, as in
  wireguard-tools reresolve-dns) while the app has traffic to send,
  or
- if a periodic check through the tunnel (ping/HTTP) fails
  N times in a row,
then recreate the socket and re-handshake — the same as a manual
reconnect. Configurable interval and on/off switch.

Similar features exist in other clients: WG Tunnel ("Restart
tunnel on ping failure"), mihomo-based clients (fallback groups
with health checks).

Server-side keepalive does not help here: we tried
PersistentKeepalive 25 on the server for this peer — the server
cannot reach the phone after the operator's NAT mapping changes,
only the phone can recover by sending first.

Thank you for AmneziaVPN!

issues.title: fix(macOS): pre-resolve Xray endpoint before tunnel setup
issues.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3132.

On macOS, Xray connections that use a domain name as the server endpoint can get stuck after the tunnel and DNS routing are configured.

The client already resolves the server hostname before starting Xray and stores the result in `m_remoteAddress`, but the native Xray config still contains the original hostname in:

`outbounds[*].settings.vnext[*].address`

As a result, Xray performs another DNS lookup after tunnel setup has started. On macOS this can cause the lookup to be routed through the tunnel itself, creating a DNS deadlock.

## Fix

Before starting Xray on macOS, create a runtime copy of the Xray config and replace only:

`outbounds[*].settings.vnext[*].address`

when it matches the original server hostname.

The resolved IP is used only for the runtime Xray configuration.

The stored profile is not modified.

## Why not use a global string replacement

PR #814 previously implemented Xray pre-resolution using a global hostname-to-IP string replacement.

That approach can also replace the same hostname when it is used as TLS/REALITY SNI, for example:

`streamSettings.realitySettings.serverName`

This patch updates only the actual connection endpoint and leaves `serverName` unchanged.

Example:

Before:

```json
{
  "address": "vpn.example.org",
  "realitySettings": {
    "serverName": "vpn.example.org"
  }
}

Runtime config after this patch:

{
  "address": "203.0.113.10",
  "realitySettings": {
    "serverName": "vpn.example.org"
  }
}
Expected behavior
hostname is resolved before tunnel setup;
Xray connects directly to the resolved IP;
REALITY/TLS SNI remains the original hostname;
the saved configuration still contains the hostname;
a new DNS resolution is performed on the next connection, so DDNS continues to work.
Scope

The change is limited to macOS runtime Xray configuration.

No routing logic, stored configuration format, or REALITY/TLS settings are changed.

Validation

The behavior matches the A/B test reported in #3132:

domain in vnext.address -> connection stalls;
pre-resolved IPv4 in vnext.address, with the same REALITY serverName -> connection works immediately.

The change is intentionally small and limited to the runtime Xray config.

issues.title: fix: handle large Linux route dumps
issues.body:
## Summary
- read multipart Linux route dumps without overflowing the original 8 KiB buffer
- select only the IPv4 default route from matching netlink responses
- skip empty WireGuard endpoint addresses and fail activation when endpoint exclusion cannot be installed
- add a Linux regression test for default-gateway discovery

## Root cause
On systems with a larger routing table, such as Ubuntu 24.04 with container or bridge routes, the `RTM_GETROUTE` dump exceeded the fixed 8192-byte buffer. The receive loop then failed before parsing the existing default route. `LinuxRouteMonitor` consequently skipped the VPN endpoint exclusion route, after which the `/1` full-tunnel routes sent the WireGuard transport back into `amn0`.

An empty IPv6 endpoint was also passed to `IPAddress`, producing the unrelated `/999999` warning.

## Validation
- reproduced with AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 / `amnezia-awg2` on Ubuntu 24.04
- regression test passed on Ubuntu 24.04 with 300 additional routes, making the dump larger than the original 8 KiB buffer
- `git diff --check` passes
- verified that the broad routing implementation remains unchanged; this is a focused hotfix

issues.title: fix(xray): pin the server endpoint to the pre-resolved address
issues.body:
## Problem

On desktop, an XRay config whose server is a host name (`vless://…@vpn.example.com:443?…&sni=vpn.example.com`, typical for imported native configs) connects but passes no traffic.

`XrayProtocol` already resolves the host before the tunnel is set up (`m_remoteAddress`) and uses that address for routes, but the XRay config still contains the host name in `outbounds[*].settings.vnext[*].address`. XRay resolves it again for every new outbound connection, after the system DNS has been switched to the tunnel's resolvers. The query goes into the tunnel, which needs a connection to the server to answer it: a deadlock.

Observed on Linux (Linux Mint 22.3, 5.0.3.0): right after connecting, tun2socks queues hundreds of connections to the local XRay inbound while XRay holds only the few server connections opened before the DNS switch; the logs show the server host queried every 5 s without an answer. On disconnect the resolver is restored, all queued lookups succeed at once and XRay opens a burst of connections.

#3165 fixes the same deadlock on macOS (#3132); the root cause is not macOS-specific.

## Fix

Before starting XRay, `start()` builds a runtime copy of the config in which every outbound endpoint (`vnext` and `servers`) whose address equals the server host name points at the pre-resolved address. If such an outbound uses TLS or REALITY without an explicit `serverName`, the host name is written there, so the SNI (and the transport host derived from it) is not replaced by the IP. The stored profile is not modified; configs that already use an IP are left as they are.

## Validation

- Built on `dev` with `-DAMNEZIA_BUILD_TESTS=ON`, `ctest` passes.
- An earlier revision of the same change on top of 5.0.3.0 (same address pinning; it also filled the transport `host` fields and logged the addresses), installed on Linux Mint 22.3: a VLESS + REALITY + Vision profile with a domain endpoint now carries traffic; the log shows one pinned outbound, XRay's server connections go out over the uplink interface and their number matches the tunneled connections.
- Not tested on Windows and macOS.

Note: on a Linux machine with Docker the connection also needs the default-gateway fix from #3231 / #3170; without it the service does not bind XRay's sockets to the uplink interface and the traffic loops into `tun2` regardless of this change.
```

issues.title: Windows XRay selects disconnected adapter with stale default gateway
issues.body:
Environment:
- AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5
- Windows 11 build 26200
- XRay core 26.7.28
- Active Ethernet connection
- Disconnected Wi-Fi adapter retaining an IPv4 address and default route

Problem:
XRay appears connected, but DNS resolution and web browsing fail. An Android client using the same server works correctly.

Observed diagnostics:
- The tun2 adapter is created successfully at 10.33.0.2.
- DNS servers 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1 are assigned to tun2.
- TCP/443 connections through tun2 succeed.
- UDP/53 requests through tun2 time out.
- TCP/53 requests through tun2 fail or are closed.
- tun2 reports traffic with no adapter packet errors or discarded packets.
- Authenticated requests directly through Amnezia's embedded SOCKS/XRay endpoint fail after successful SOCKS authentication.
- A server-side packet capture receives the Windows XRay connection but sees no corresponding outbound DNS or web traffic.
- Server-side TCP and UDP DNS tests through the same VLESS/Reality configuration succeed.
- The Windows and server XRay core versions are both 26.7.28.

Root-cause indication:
NetworkUtilities::getGatewayAndIface() enumerates adapters returned by GetAdaptersAddresses() and retains the last adapter containing an IPv4 gateway. It does not check OperStatus and does not select the best route.

Xray::startXray() then uses that interface index with IP_UNICAST_IF for every outbound XRay socket.

The disconnected Wi-Fi adapter still had an IPv4 address and an active default route. Disabling Wi-Fi at the adapter level removed that route and immediately made XRay work.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Connect Windows to the internet through Ethernet.
2. Leave a Wi-Fi adapter disconnected but retaining an IPv4 address and default route.
3. Connect an XRay Reality profile in AmneziaVPN.
4. Observe that Amnezia reports a connection, but DNS and web browsing fail.
5. Disable the Wi-Fi adapter with Disable-NetAdapter.
6. Reconnect AmneziaVPN.
7. Observe that DNS and web browsing now work.

Expected behavior:
Amnezia should select the active adapter used by the best route to the VPN server.

Suggested fix:
Use GetBestRoute/GetBestRoute2 for the VPN server address, or ignore adapters whose OperStatus is not IfOperStatusUp. Do not select the last adapter returned by GetAdaptersAddresses().

Workaround:
Disable disconnected adapters that retain default gateways.

issues.title: Updating/recreating an existing AmneziaWG protocol doesn't install the required kernel DKMS module
issues.body:
Problem:

On a self-hosted server (Ubuntu, Docker-based A-VPN setup), when trying to update an existing AmneziaWG protocol (not a fresh install, but an upgrade/recreation of an already existing one) through the desktop client, the Docker container is created, but the WireGuard interface inside it doesn't come up. On investigation, the cause turned out to be the absence of a suitable kernel DKMS module (amneziawg) on the host, either outdated or completely missing after the reinstall.

The client doesn't check for or install the module as part of the update process, so the container ends up stuck in a non-functional state (just "tail -f /dev/null" inside) with no visible error in the UI (the app just shows "Connecting..." indefinitely).

A broader scenario worth considering:

A single server can have not just the containerized A-VPN, but also a separate, independent "native" AmneziaWG installation (not through Docker, using the same kernel module directly). We had both present on our server at the same time, for different purposes. The client doesn't check whether a native AmneziaWG is already installed on the host separately from the Docker container, and this creates a version conflict between what the container needs and what's already installed and in use outside the container. We ran into this directly: having both installations at once is exactly what caused the described problem. This could be a source of similar issues for other users who use their server for multiple purposes, not just A-VPN.

What fixed it:

A full server reinstall through the "Automatic" option (the same path used when adding a completely new, clean server) worked correctly and installed the module as part of the process, but only after we manually removed both the containerized and the native AmneziaWG installations from the server entirely. So the problem is specific to the "update/recreate existing protocol" path on a server that already had something installed, not to installing on a genuinely clean server.

Also noticed:

During this process we also noticed that when the protocol is recreated, the new random port chosen by the container isn't automatically added to the server's firewall (UFW), so even with a working WireGuard interface, the connection would still be unreachable from outside without manually adding a rule.

Request:

Please check and unify both paths (fresh install and updating an existing protocol), so that updating also includes checking/installing system dependencies (the kernel module) and configuring the firewall for the new port. It would also help to explicitly detect and handle the case where a non-Docker-based AmneziaWG installation is already present on the server, to avoid module version conflicts.

issues.title: fix(windows): eliminate route-change storms with large split-tunnel e…
issues.body:
…xclusion lists

Importing a large IP exclusion list (~8.6k prefixes) made the Windows client unusable: connecting stalled for many minutes, disconnecting hung, and after a forced kill the client could not reconnect until reboot.

Three related defects in WindowsRouteMonitor:

1. Quadratic route installation. Every added exclusion route refetched the full routing table and interface metrics. Measured on stock: 500 prefixes = 1.4s, 1000 = 6.4s, 2000 = 33.4s (the kernel itself installs 500 routes in 146ms). Fix: batched add/delete entry points that snapshot the table once per address family; the teardown loop additionally refetched the table per deleted prefix.

2. Self-sustaining rescan storm. The monitor subscribes to NotifyRouteChange2, but its own rescan rewrites routes (captured clones, flapping next-hops), waking itself: with a large list the monitor rescanned ~4 times/second for the whole session, starving the IPC queue (deactivate took minutes to be processed). The callback filter cannot drop these notifications because the notification rows carry unreliable Protocol/Metric fields. Fix: unsubscribe for the duration of bulk operations and of the rescan itself, then run exactly one manual rescan; real network changes still trigger it via the restored subscription.

3. Orphaned exclusion routes. After a hard service kill the routes stayed in the system table pointing at the dead tunnel's next-hop, blackholing matching traffic (including the VPN server handshake) until reboot. Fix: purge NETMGMT+EXCLUSION_ROUTE_METRIC rows at monitor creation - that pair is only ever produced by this code.

Result with an 8658-prefix list: connect in 4-7s (route installation 0.85s), idle monitor after connect, teardown in seconds, reboot no longer needed after a crash.

comments.issue_title: fix(macOS): pre-resolve Xray endpoint before tunnel setup
comments.body:
The same deadlock happens on Linux (Linux Mint 22.3, 5.0.3.0, VLESS + REALITY with a domain endpoint): once the system DNS is switched to the tunnel, XRay's lookup of the server host goes into the tunnel and never returns; tun2socks piles up connections while XRay holds only the few opened before the switch.

So the `#ifdef Q_OS_MACOS` guard could probably be dropped. One more detail: when an outbound uses TLS without an explicit `serverName`, replacing the address with the IP also makes XRay send the IP as SNI, so the host name should be written to `serverName` in that case.

I opened #3362 with a cross-platform version of this change (vnext and servers, plus the `serverName` fallback). Happy to close it if you prefer to extend this PR instead.

comments.issue_title: fix: handle large Linux route dumps
comments.body:
Confirming on Linux Mint 22.3 with Docker (about a dozen bridge networks), AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0, and with the **XRay** protocol, not only WireGuard/AWG.

Without the multipart route dump `getGatewayAndIface()` returns nothing, so the client never logs `Gateway … for interface …` and the service never logs `using uplink interface`. The service then does not bind XRay's sockets to the uplink interface (`SO_BINDTODEVICE` in `Xray::sockCallback`), XRay's connections to the server fall under the `/1` routes into `tun2`, and tun2socks hands them back to XRay: a few seconds after connecting there were ~28,000 "established" connections to the server address and no traffic.

With the full route dump read (same approach as this PR and #3170) the gateway is found, XRay's sockets go out over the uplink interface and the connection works.

Correction to my comment above, Case 2 (sleep at home, wake at the office): the endpoint route is **not** the explanation there. Case 1 (route left on an unplugged adapter) stands as measured.

I captured the next occurrence with `pktmon` (2026-10-30, AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0, wake at the office, tunnel process survived sleep):

- The endpoint route was correct: `<server>/32` via the Ethernet gateway, Ethernet up.
- At the Ethernet adapter, the tunnel's UDP packets left with the correct source (`10.0.6.43:53780 → <server>:<port>`, correct gateway MAC): about 4,100 packets in 22 s, **0 packets from the server on any interface**.
- At the same time, TCP from the same interface to `<server>` (ports 443 and 22) worked.
- Reconnecting created a new socket (source port 53780 → 63024). The handshake completed 1.6 s after `activate`, on the same adapter, the same gateway, and the same server port. In the next 20 s: about 13,000 packets out and about 21,000 in.

So the old UDP flow stopped getting any answer, while a new flow from the same address worked immediately. The packets leave the laptop correctly, so this looks like something outside the client: on the path, or on the server.

Pattern since 2026-10-23, from the service log:
- 4 of 4 wakes at the office failed. In each, the handshake first succeeds over office Wi-Fi, and 9–20 s after the wake the wired adapter comes up (or, today, resets).
- 0 of 7 wakes at home failed (single Wi-Fi network).
- Two of the four failures used a tunnel process started at home, whose port had never been used on the office network. So it is not stale NAT state left over from the previous day.
- The `stopped hearing back after N seconds` timer is armed by the first packet sent after the last one received, and outgoing traffic was continuous. So it dates the last received packet:
  - 10-28: within 1 s of the wired adapter coming up;
  - 10-29: within 1 s of the wired adapter coming up;
  - 10-30: 1 s after the handshake, while the wired adapter was still resetting.
- In every case, only a manual reconnect fixed it. `UDP bind has been updated` appears only at activation (7 of 7), never on a network change.

A possible client-side mitigation: when the default-route interface changes and nothing is received for a few seconds, re-handshake on a fresh UDP socket (new source port) instead of retrying on the old one. This is what a manual reconnect does.
